You can set a limit on the number of characters in the full file name. The full file name includes: the folder names, the path separators, the file name, and the extension.

The default value is `210`, and the maximum value is `250`. If the number of characters in the full file name exceeds the set value, the downloader truncates the file name first, so that the number of characters is less than the set value. If necessary, it also truncates the folder names.

**Why limit the file name length?**

If the name of a file or folder is too long, the browser may not be able to save the file automatically, and will show a "Save As" window for the user to save it manually. This not only affects the user experience, but if the user does not act in time, it also causes the download progress to get stuck.

After enabling this setting, the downloader checks the number of characters in the full file name (including all folders and the file name). If it exceeds the length limit, some characters are truncated, so that the browser can save the file automatically and no longer shows the "Save As" window.

**Why might a file name be too long?**

Some tags in the naming rule may output a lot of text, which may cause the length of the file name to exceed the length allowed by the operating system (usually no more than 256 characters).

Two kinds of tags easily cause this problem: one is the title, including `{title}` and `{page_title}`, because the titles of some novels are very long. The other is the tag list, including `{tags}`, `{tags_translate}`, `{tags_transl_only}` and `{page_tag}`, because some tags contain many characters.

?> It is not recommended to set this value too large. Sometimes `210` may still be too large. If you encounter problems, you can reduce this value.
